prf:shell-closure-stability:
Proof Proof of shell closure stability. Scope of the dual-lift argument. Step 1 below contains an open gap: in the dual matrix inequality u_0 I + \sum_\lambda u_\lambda \pi_\lambda - T \preceq 0 with u_\lambda \ge 0, increasing a newly introduced multiplier u_\lambda adds a positive semidefinite term and tightens the inequality rather than relaxing it. The least restrictive choice on a new block is u_\lambda = 0, for which the dual lift is feasible only when u_0 I \preceq T_{\mathrm{new}} on that block—a domination bound not established here. Consequently, claim 1 of the proposition (and the monotonicity clause of claim 2 that rests on it) remains conditional on that block-domination bound, while step 3 compares the shell gap against the Archimedean quantity \alpha \cdot m_e \cdot c_q^2 across the evaluation wall.

One establishes three claims.

1. SDP-relaxation monotonicity. At each step Z - 1 \to Z, the dressing morphism \mathrm{dress}_{S_Z} induces a cabling embedding \iota: H_{A + Z - 1}(q) \hookrightarrow H_{A + Z}(q). Three structural changes follow in the confinement SDP:

(a) Primal relaxation. The primal variable space extends from \mathrm{End}_R(H_{A+Z-1}(R, q)) to \mathrm{End}_R(H_{A+Z}(R, q)). The cabling-induced lift \Phi \mapsto \iota_* \Phi \oplus 0 embeds every primal-feasible point of \mathrm{SDP}_{Z-1} into the primal-feasible set of \mathrm{SDP}_Z, preserving the objective \langle T, \Phi \rangle.

(b) Dual relaxation. Dual variables extend by new shadow prices u_\lambda \ge 0 for every Wedderburn block \lambda \vdash k with k \in \{A+Z-1+1,\ldots, A+Z\} that first becomes available. Setting these new variables to zero recovers the old dual feasibility condition. Every dual-feasible point of \mathrm{SDP}_{Z-1} admits a lift to a dual-feasible point of \mathrm{SDP}_Z achieving the same objective n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot u_0.

(c) Cost compatibility. The cost operator extends as a direct sum T^{(Z)} = \iota_* T^{(Z-1)} \oplus T_{\mathrm{new}}, where T_{\mathrm{new}} is the Markov-trace weight on the new block. Feasibility of the dual lift requires only that the additional u_\lambda^{(Z)} on the new blocks dominate T_{\mathrm{new}} in the matrix inequality u_0 I + \sum u_\lambda \pi_\lambda - T \preceq 0. Because T_{\mathrm{new}} is bounded and the new u_\lambda can take any non-negative value, a dominating choice always exists.

Because \mathrm{SDP}_Z maximises the dual objective over a superset of feasible points containing the lift of (u_0^{(Z-1)}, u_\lambda^{(Z-1)}), standard SDP-relaxation monotonicity gives

  \sigma_F(P^{(Z)}, q)
  \;=\;
  n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot u_0^{*(Z)}
  \;\ge\;
  n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot u_0^{*(Z-1)}
  \;=\;
  \sigma_F(P^{(Z-1)}, q).

(Cost compatibility makes the lift feasible, ensuring the relaxation argument holds despite constraints added by dressing).

2. Local maxima. For Z \in \mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{noble}}, the orbital parametrisation of the electron shell fills all magnetic and spin labels of principal shell n. Multiple Wedderburn blocks of the multi-level SDP are simultaneously tight: \mu(S_Z, q) \ge 2. Simultaneous tightness means the active-support Gram matrix has a rank-\mu dual kernel. By confinement-topological, the corresponding Frobenius form is non-degenerate on the complementary subspace (the complement is taken inside H_n/\mathrm{rad} \cong \mathrm{TL}_n, since the radical blocks are degenerate for the trace and would otherwise sit in every complement), and its minimum eigenvalue strictly exceeds the single-block value. This shell-boundary spectral-gap jump equals the strict local maximum of the marginal gain \Delta\sigma_F; \sigma_F itself stays monotone.

3. Terminality. An outgoing dressing \mathrm{dress}_{S'}: P^{(Z)} \to P' with Z \in \mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{noble}} extends the active support by opening a block of principal shell n + 1. Because the n-th shell is fully closed, no dual variable in shell n can slack. The extension is feasible only if every dual variable in shell n increases; every currently tight block must break to admit the new one. The energetic cost of breaking \mu(S_Z, q) \ge 2 tight blocks is at least \mu \cdot \Delta E_{\mathrm{shell}}(q). For q in the generic locus, \mu \cdot \Delta E_{\mathrm{shell}}(q) > \alpha \cdot m_e \cdot c_q^2. No electromagnetic-mediated dressing clears the barrier, making P^{(Z)} terminal within the \mathrm{dress} sub-diagram. \square

prop:level-sufficiency:
Proposition Level sufficiency: Markov trace computable in the coarsest confinement algebra. Let P = (\mathrm{name}, \ell, [K]_M, n_0) be a confined particle and let

  \uparrow_\ell \colon P \longrightarrow P^{\uparrow}
  \quad\text{with}\quad
  P^{\uparrow} = (\mathrm{name}, \ell - 1, [\iota(K)]_M, n_1)

be an unfolding morphism in the confinement category, where \iota: H_{n_0}(R, q) \hookrightarrow H_{n_1}(R, q) is the Hecke inclusion and n_1 \ge n_0. If the coarse witnessed partition truncation satisfies

  k_{\max}(P, q) \le n_0

then the Markov trace is preserved along the unfolding:

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\left(T_w^{\downarrow}\right)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\left(T_w^{\uparrow}\right)
  \quad\text{in }\mathbb{C}(q),

where T_w^{\downarrow} \in H_{n_0}(q) and T_w^{\uparrow} \in H_{n_1}(q) are the Gröbner–Shirshov normal forms of K at coarse and fine levels respectively. Consequently, every trace-class invariant \mathcal{F} of P takes the same value on P and P^{\uparrow}:

  \mathcal{F}(P) \;=\; \mathcal{F}(P^{\uparrow}).

The coarsest level at which k_{\max}(P, q, n) \le n is computationally sufficient. Unfolding to any deeper level is superfluous for trace-class invariants.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs. Any generic categorical identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
prf:level-sufficiency:
Proof Proof of level sufficiency. The Ocneanu–Jones Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M: H_\bullet(q) \to \mathbb{C}(q) is a compatible family along the Hecke tower H_n(R, q) \hookrightarrow H_{n+1}(R, q). It satisfies the Markov property \mathrm{tr}_M \circ \iota = \mathrm{tr}_M (Jones 1987). Hypothesis k_{\max}(P, q) \le n_0 asserts that every Wedderburn block \lambda \vdash k with k > n_0 has zero projection in T_w^{\downarrow}. Under the inclusion \iota: H_{n_0}(R, q) \hookrightarrow H_{n_1}(R, q) this vanishing is preserved. The additional blocks \lambda \vdash k with n_0 < k \le n_1 accessible at the fine level contribute zero to T_w^{\uparrow} = \iota\,T_w^{\downarrow}. Thus \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w^{\uparrow}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\iota\,T_w^{\downarrow}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w^{\downarrow}) by the Markov property. Functoriality of \mathrm{tr}_M: \mathbf{Conf} \to \mathbb{C}(q) (confinement category) extends this equality to every composite of unfoldings, establishing preservation along the full confinement chain.

For a general trace-class invariant \mathcal{F} that factors through \mathrm{tr}_M, equality of traces implies equality of values: \mathcal{F}(P^{\uparrow}) = \mathcal{F}(P). \square

Converse (unfolding necessity). If k_{\max}(P, q) > n_0 — the witnessed partition content of P exceeds the coarse strand count — then no representation of T_w^{\downarrow} as an element of H_{n_0}(q) captures all tight dual blocks of the confinement SDP. Unfolding to the smallest level n_1 with k_{\max}(P, q, n_1) \le n_1 is strictly required. The unfolded trace \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w^{\uparrow}) differs from any coarse surrogate by contributions from the additional blocks. Magic shell closure and multi-operator binding configurations (\mu(S, q) \ge 2) are the principal triggers.

Corollary (default-coarse computability). Every trace-class invariant \mathcal{F} computed at the coarsest level satisfying k_{\max} \le n is exact. Default-coarse computation is not a performance heuristic. It is the content of this proposition.
rem:level-sufficiency-interprets:

At each level, any trace-class invariant is exact at the coarsest representation satisfying k_{\max}(P, q, n_0) \le n_0.

  1. Identify the confined particle P at its natural level \ell.
  2. Read k_{\max}(P, q, n_0) from the witness data.
  3. If k_{\max}(P, q, n_0) \le n_0, compute \mathrm{tr}_M at the coarse level and halt.
  4. If k_{\max}(P, q, n_0) > n_0, apply the unfolding morphism \uparrow_\ell and repeat at \ell - 1.

  • Magic shell closure. Atoms at A \in \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\} and noble-gas electron counts Z \in \{2, 10, 18, 36, 54, 86\} exhibit binding multiplicity \mu(S, q) \ge 2. This forces k_{\max} above the coarse count. Atoms in these rows evaluate one level deeper.
  • SDP cross-channel demand. The active dual support \mathcal{S}^* of the confinement SDP spans blocks \lambda_1, \lambda_2. When \max(|\lambda_1|, |\lambda_2|) > n_0, the coarse representation cannot express the coupling. Unfolding is required.

Non-magic atoms and molecules without SDP cross-channel demand evaluate at their natural coarse level. This is the minimal exact representation.

Dressing preserves computational minimality. Under the dressing morphism \mathrm{dress}_S: P_{\mathrm{bare}} \to P_{\mathrm{dressed}}, the witnessed truncation updates to

  k_{\max}(P_{\mathrm{dressed}}, q)
  \;=\;
  \max\bigl(k_{\max}(P_{\mathrm{bare}}, q),\;
            k_{\max}^{\mathrm{bind}}(S, q)\bigr),

where k_{\max}^{\mathrm{bind}} is the partition reach of the binding subword W_{\mathrm{bind}}. The dressed particle's computational level follows from the updated k_{\max}. Adding a single electron to a non-magic atom typically leaves the computational level unchanged. Closing to a noble gas triggers \mu \ge 2 and raises the required level.

Default-coarse computation is the computational content of this proposition applied via the confinement category.
prop:confinement-phase-stratification:
Proposition The confinement locus is open, and the active support is constant on a strictly complementary phase. Let P be a confined particle, and let the aether parameter q range over \mathbb{R}_{>1}. Write strict feasibility of the confinement SDP as a finite system of strict inequalities 0 < g_i(q, X), i \in I, in q and the decision variable X, with each g_i continuous. (Positive definiteness of a Gram matrix is such a system, by Sylvester's criterion on its leading principal minors.) The confinement locus of P is

  \Omega(P) \;:=\; \{\, q : \exists X,\ \forall i \in I,\ 0 < g_i(q, X) \,\}.

Let u^*_\lambda(q) be the dual variables of the SDP and s_\lambda(q) the matching primal slacks. The active support is \mathcal{S}^*(P, q) := \{\lambda : u^*_\lambda(q) > 0\} and the binding multiplicity is \mu(P, q) := |\mathcal{S}^*(P, q)|. Then:

  1. Openness. \Omega(P) is open.
  2. Constancy on a phase. Let C \subseteq \Omega(P) be connected. Suppose u^*_\lambda and s_\lambda are continuous in q, complementary (u^*_\lambda s_\lambda = 0) and strictly complementary (u^*_\lambda > 0 or s_\lambda > 0) at every q \in C. Then \mathcal{S}^*(P, q) and \mu(P, q) are constant on C.

The remaining structure of the phases (the boundary stratification, analyticity of the Frobenius stability index, scope and phase transitions) is stated separately in the phase-boundary conjecture below.

Archimedean specialisation. Both parts sit on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall: the locus is a subset of \mathbb{R}, and openness and connectedness are statements about the real topology.
prf:confinement-phase-stratification:
Proof Proof of confinement phase stratification. Claim (1)—Openness. Let S := \{(q, X) : \forall i,\ 0 < g_i(q, X)\}. Each set \{0 < g_i\} is open because g_i is continuous, and I is finite, so S is open. \Omega(P) is the image of S under the projection (q, X) \mapsto q, which is an open map. Hence \Omega(P) is open.

Claim (2)—Constancy on a phase. Fix \lambda. Let U := \{q : u^*_\lambda(q) > 0\} and V := \{q : s_\lambda(q) > 0\}; both are open by continuity. Strict complementarity gives C \subseteq U \cup V. If C met both U and V, then, C being connected, it would meet U \cap V at some q; there u^*_\lambda(q)\, s_\lambda(q) > 0, contradicting complementarity. So either u^*_\lambda > 0 on all of C, or u^*_\lambda > 0 nowhere on C. This holds for every \lambda, so \mathcal{S}^*(P, q) is the same set for every q \in C, and so is its size \mu(P, q). \square
rem:confinement-phase-stratification-int: Remark Topology of the confinement locus \Omega(P). For simple particles, \Omega(P) is expected to be a single connected interval of \mathbb{R}_{>1} containing q_0; neither connectedness nor q_0 \in \Omega(P) is proved. For composite particles with multi-block binding, \Omega(P) can be disconnected. Each component corresponds to a distinct configuration of the active support. One physically realises transitions between components as chemical or nuclear rearrangements. Computationally, they appear as regime switches in the witness files.
conj:confinement-phase-boundaries:
Conjecture Phase boundaries of the confinement locus. Let P be a confined particle, with confinement locus \Omega(P), active support \mathcal{S}^*(P, q), binding multiplicity \mu(P, q) and Frobenius stability index \sigma_F(P, q) as in prop:confinement-phase-stratification. Let \mathcal{G} \subset \mathbb{R}_{>1} be the generic locus of q, and call a connected component \Omega_\alpha of \Omega(P) a confinement phase. Then:

  1. Stratification. The complement \mathcal{G} \setminus \Omega(P) is a real-algebraic stratification with strata of codimension \ge 1, the phase boundaries of P. Each stratum is the zero locus of a principal minor of the SDP Gram matrix.
  2. Strict complementarity on phases. On each phase \Omega_\alpha the SDP dual pair is continuous and strictly complementary, so the active support and \mu are constant on \Omega_\alpha by prop:confinement-phase-stratification.
  3. Analyticity. \sigma_F(P, q) is real-analytic on each \Omega_\alpha.
  4. Scope. Level sufficiency, shell-closure stability and the Markov-trace preservation of the confinement category functor hold pointwise in each \Omega_\alpha and fail on \partial\Omega(P).
  5. Phase transitions. If a continuous path q: [0, 1] \to \mathcal{G} crosses a phase boundary at q_0 \in \partial\Omega(P), then at q_0 either P is not realisable as a closed-braid bound state (deconfinement), or \mu jumps, the active support gains or loses a Wedderburn block, and \sigma_F has a non-smooth point (regime switch), or both.

Supporting argument (not a proof). For (1): the entries of the Gram matrix are Laurent polynomials in q, so each principal minor that is not identically zero has finitely many real zeros in \mathcal{G}; what is not shown is that loss of strict feasibility happens exactly on these zero sets. For (2): strict complementarity holds for generic SDP data (Alizadeh–Haeberly–Overton), but genericity at the aether parameters is not established. For (4): the proofs of prop:level-sufficiency and prop:shell-closure-stability use a well-defined, locally constant active support. For (5): a boundary crossing is either a loss of strict primal feasibility or a dual variable u^*_\lambda passing through zero.
rem:phase-scoped-applicability:
Remark Phase-scoped applicability: confinement theorems hold on open strata only. The phase-boundary conjecture (conj:confinement-phase-boundaries) proposes the scope caveat attached to every statement in the confinement framework. Any formal statement about a confined particle P, its electron shell, a dressing morphism, or a trace-class invariant \mathcal{F}(P) includes the implicit quantifier:

  \forall\, q \in \Omega_\alpha(P),

where \Omega_\alpha(P) is a fixed connected component of the confinement locus \Omega(P), a single confinement phase.

Conjecturally phase-scoped results (conjectured to hold only within a single \Omega_\alpha):

  • Level sufficiency: preservation of Markov trace under unfolding.
  • Shell-closure stability: monotonicity of \sigma_F along the dressing chain and local maxima at noble-gas Z.
  • Functoriality of \mathrm{tr}_M: \mathbf{Conf} \to \mathbb{C}(q).
  • Multi-operator binding structure: constancy of the active support.

Boundary phenomena (not covered by the phase-scoped results):

  • Deconfinement events. At q \in \partial\Omega(P) with Slater-strict feasibility lost, P ceases to be realisable as a closed-braid bound state.
  • Regime switches. At q \in \partial\Omega(P) with a \mu-jump but preserved feasibility, the active support gains or loses a Wedderburn block.
  • Critical scaling. Near a phase boundary, \sigma_F typically has a non-analytic limit.
  • Chemical and nuclear rearrangements. Transitions between disconnected components of \Omega(P) for a composite P are realised physically as structural rearrangements. These transitions require an explicit cross-component analysis using the stratification of \Omega(P).

Practical reading. When encountering a confinement-framework statement, treat q as ranging over a fixed open phase unless the text addresses boundary behaviour. Numerical witnesses evaluate at a single q = q_0 \approx 1.110. As long as that point lies in \Omega_\alpha(P), the phase-scoped results apply wherever they hold. Auditing behaviour across q ranges requires explicit stratification analysis.

prop:lp-dual-stability:

def:algebraic-primality:
Definition Algebraic primality of a strand count. Fix an aether parameter q > 1. For each strand count n \geq 1, the confinement SDP selects a canonical state \psi_n(q). Say that n is algebraically prime at q if \psi_n(q) is not contained in the closed span of any non-trivial tensor product

  \overline{\mathrm{span}}\bigl\{\,
    \psi_{n_1}(q) \otimes \cdots \otimes \psi_{n_k}(q)
  \,\bigr\}.

This product is indexed by a decomposition n = n_1 + \cdots + n_k with k \geq 2 and every n_i \geq 1.
rem:algebraic-primality-remark:
Remark Algebraic primality as a magic-number surrogate. By convention, n = 0 is not prime. This predicate serves as a purely algebraic surrogate for a magic strand count. An algebraically prime configuration does not factor into a product of smaller closed configurations.

The definition relies on a recursive decomposition argument. Testing primality at n checks all decompositions into smaller parts. The recursion bottoms out at n = 1. The n=1 state is algebraically prime vacuously, because no decomposition into k \geq 2 positive parts sums to 1.
prop:n-equals-1-vacuous-magic:

Equivalently, the canonical state \psi_1(q) is not in the closed span of any non-trivial tensor product of canonical states indexed by a decomposition 1 = n_1 + \cdots + n_k with k \geq 2 and n_i \geq 1. No such decomposition exists.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall.
rem:n-equals-1-vacuous-magic-context:
Remark Base case, empirical magic numbers, and archimedean scope of vacuous primality. The proof uses only elementary arithmetic. It uses no SDP analysis, Hecke-algebra machinery, or tensor-product manipulation. This is the base case of the recursion. Every primality check at n \geq 2 ultimately bottoms out at n = 1 through repeated decomposition.

Empirical nuclear magic numbers start at 2. The framework's n = 1 primality is sometimes glossed as below the lowest shell closure. Within the algebraic-primality framework, n = 1 is strictly magic, just for a vacuous reason.

The archimedean specialisation invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs. Any generic categorical identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
prf:n-equals-1-vacuous-magic:
Proof Proof of n equals 1 vacuous magic. The claim reduces to a vacuous-truth statement about positive-integer decompositions.

  1. Suppose, for contradiction, that a decomposition 1 = n_1 + n_2 + \cdots + n_k exists with k \geq 2 and n_i \geq 1 for all i = 1, \ldots, k.
  2. Lower-bound the sum: 
      \sum_{i=1}^{k} n_i \;\geq\; \sum_{i=1}^{k} 1 \;=\; k \;\geq\; 2.
  3. By hypothesis \sum_{i=1}^{k} n_i = 1, so 1 \geq 2. Contradiction.
  4. Therefore no decomposition with k \geq 2 and all n_i \geq 1 summing to 1 exists.
  5. The universal-quantifier statement "\psi_1(q) \notin \overline{\mathrm{span}}\{\cdots\} for every such decomposition" ranges over the empty set of decompositions and is vacuously true.

Therefore 1 is algebraically prime at every q > 1. \square

sec:nn-isospin-interface-intro:
Four two-nucleon states exist in nature: the three isospin-triplet (T = 1) states (pp, nn, and the symmetric pn configuration), none of which forms a bound state, and the unique isospin-singlet (T = 0) antisymmetric pn state—the deuteron—which binds at 2.224566\;\mathrm{MeV}. A first-principles theory of nuclear interactions must account for both the discrete selection of the T = 0 channel and the numerical value of its binding energy.

Two distinct algebraic mechanisms operate on the two-nucleon braid, and maintaining their separation is essential:

  1. Isospin channel selection: Each two-nucleon isospin channel carries the Wedderburn weight of its symmetry block, \mu_+ for the symmetric triplet and \mu_- for the antisymmetric singlet. At the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1), the strict inequality \mu_- < \mu_+ holds identically for all q > 1. Because the logarithmic binding functional B = -\alpha\log\mu is strictly decreasing in \mu, the isospin singlet T = 0 is unconditionally more strongly bound than the triplet T = 1 without parameter tuning.
  2. Interface bond evaluation: In the composite mass pipeline, an inter-nucleon bond contributes a Markov scalar \mu = z + d with deformation parameter d \in [-h, 0], from which the quantitative binding energy is extracted via the same logarithmic functional.

This section proves the universal ordering \mu_- < \mu_+, refutes the naive content-keyed interface alternative, defines the isospin selection map on colour systems, and establishes the branching identity tying the isospin weights to H_n(q). Measuring the admissible interface band [z - h, z] against \mu_- and \mu_+ reveals that the interface interval lies strictly between the two Wedderburn weights (\mu_- < z - h < z < \mu_+), proving that channel selection and bond magnitude operate on disjoint algebraic strata, while the \mathrm{SO}(3) spin fibre and spin–isospin product generate Wigner's \mathrm{SU}(4) supermultiplet symmetry.
prop:isospin-singlet-binds-more:
Proposition \mu_- < \mu_+ for every q>0 at z = q^3/(q^2+1): the isospin singlet is always the more strongly bound channel. Let z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) be the Markov parameter and let

  \mu_+ \;=\; \frac{z + q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}},
  \qquad
  \mu_- \;=\; \frac{q - z}{q + q^{-1}}

be the interface scalars of the isospin triplet and singlet. Then

  \boxed{\;\; \mu_- \;<\; \mu_+ \qquad \text{for every } q > 0. \;\;}

The ordering is forced, not fitted

The difference of the two scalars is

  \mu_+ - \mu_- \;=\; \frac{2z - h}{q + q^{-1}},
  \qquad h = q - q^{-1},

and at z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) the numerator is an identity with a manifestly positive value:

  2z - h \;=\; \frac{q^{4}+1}{q\,(q^{2}+1)} .

Every factor on the right is a sum of even powers of q divided by a product of positive terms, so the sign requires no numerical input and no estimate. The denominator q + q^{-1} is positive for q > 0 by the same reading. The ordering therefore holds for the whole positive axis, not on a window around the aether parameter.

How this ordering is read against the measured two-nucleon channels, with the values at q_0, is recorded in the two-nucleon reading.
prop:content-keyed-interface-refuted:
Proposition No interface keyed on nucleon content can work: the two pn channels share content and differ in boundness. Let \mathrm{content} : \mathrm{Channel} \to \mathrm{Content} send a two-nucleon channel to the unordered pair of nucleon species it contains, and suppose the binding energy factors through it, B = \tilde B \circ \mathrm{content}. Then no such \tilde B reproduces the observed pattern.

The argument needs one input from experiment. The two pn channels have the same content and opposite boundness: pn({}^3S_1) is the deuteron, bound at +2.224566\ \mathrm{MeV}, while pn({}^1S_0) is unbound, a virtual state at -0.066\ \mathrm{MeV}. A function of the content alone assigns them the same value. One channel must therefore be mis-assigned, whatever \tilde B is.

Scope of the refutation

This is a structural exclusion, not a scope-limited negative. The invariant forbidding the construction is named and is a property of the hypothesis class rather than of any member of it: the assumed factorisation through \mathrm{content} makes B constant on the fibres of that map, and the two pn channels lie in a single fibre with opposite signs of binding. No choice of the per-species multiplicities m_{pp}, m_{nn}, m_{pn} escapes it, and neither does any refinement that still reads only the nucleon species off the pair.

What is excluded is precisely the "identical nucleons take two crossings" proposal and every variant of it that keys the interface on species content. What is not excluded is a crossing count as such: a rule that reads the state of the pair rather than its content is untouched by the argument.

What replaces it

The variable that separates the two pn channels is the isospin label T, which distinguishes the exchange-symmetric T = 1 combination from the antisymmetric T = 0 one while leaving the species content identical. That variable is already supplied by the isospin ordering, which assigns \mu_+ to the triplet and \mu_- to the singlet and orders them without a fit.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs --- real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the aether parameter q_0. Any generic categorical or q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here. The two experimental inputs are the AME deuteron binding +2.224566\ \mathrm{MeV} and the pn({}^1S_0) virtual state at -0.066\ \mathrm{MeV}; the argument itself is a statement about the factorisation and holds over any ordered field.
rem:isospin-singlet-binds-more-two-nucle:

What it selects

Binding is B = -\alpha\log\mu with \alpha > 0, a decreasing function of \mu, so the smaller scalar is the more strongly bound channel. The singlet is thus predicted to bind harder than the triplet at every q, and nature agrees: of the four two-nucleon channels --- pp, nn and pn({}^1S_0), all T = 1, against pn({}^3S_1), the deuteron at T = 0 --- exactly the T = 0 channel binds.

The selection is made by a representation label. There is no crossing count, no per-species multiplicity m_{pp}, m_{nn}, m_{pn} to choose, and consequently nothing to tune: the channel is picked out by which isospin block of H_2(q) its weight comes from. The alternative story, in which the interface is keyed on the nucleon content of the pair, is not only unnecessary; it is unavailable --- see the content-keyed refutation.

prf:isospin-singlet-binds-more:
Proof Proof: the positive numerator, and the transport to binding energy.

The inequality

Both scalars carry the same denominator q + q^{-1}, which is positive for q > 0, and the ordering therefore reduces to the numerators: \mu_- < \mu_+ is equivalent to q - z < z + q^{-1}, that is to h < 2z with h = q - q^{-1}.

Substituting z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) and clearing denominators turns 2z - h into a closed form rather than an estimate:

  2\,\frac{q^{3}}{q^{2}+1} \;-\; \Bigl(q - \frac1q\Bigr)
  \;=\; \frac{2q^{4} - (q^{2}-1)(q^{2}+1)}{q\,(q^{2}+1)}
  \;=\; \frac{q^{4}+1}{q\,(q^{2}+1)} .

The numerator q^{4}+1 and the denominator q(q^{2}+1) are both strictly positive for q > 0, so 2z - h > 0 identically. Dividing by the common positive denominator restores the inequality on the scalars.

Nothing in the computation is specific to the aether parameter, and nothing is approximate: the quantity whose sign is at issue has been written as a ratio of positives, which is the strongest form the claim admits.

Transport to binding energy

The binding of a channel is B_T = -\alpha \log \mu_T with \alpha > 0 the energy scale. Since \log is strictly increasing on the positive reals and \mu_- > 0, the inequality \mu_- < \mu_+ gives \log \mu_- < \log \mu_+, and multiplying by -\alpha reverses it:

  B_+ \;=\; -\alpha\log\mu_+ \;<\; -\alpha\log\mu_- \;=\; B_- .

The transport step is where the argument leaves the algebra and enters the archimedean sector, since \log is a real-analytic function and the energy scale is a physical quantity. The inequality it transports, however, was established over an ordered field with no such input, so the two halves of the proof sit on opposite sides of the algebraic→archimedean wall and only the second is specialised.
prop:markov-stabilisation-needs-a-fresh-:
Proposition Markov stabilisation at the interface requires a generator the word does not already use. Let \mathbf{A} be a ring carrying a Hecke generator \sigma with \sigma^2 = h\,\sigma + 1, and let \mathrm{tr} be linear with \mathrm{tr}(1) = 1. If \mathrm{tr}(\sigma) = z and Markov stabilisation \mathrm{tr}(W\sigma) = z\,\mathrm{tr}(W) is assumed at W = \sigma, then

  z^2 = h\,z + 1 .

At z = q^3/(q^2+1) with h = q - q^{-1}, that equation has no solution: for every q > 0

  z^2 - h\,z - 1
    \;=\; -\,\frac{(q^2 - q + 1)(q^2 + q + 1)}{(q^2+1)^2}
    \;<\; 0 .

Hence stabilisation fails at a generator the word already uses.

The interface between two nucleons contributes to the Markov trace through a single element a\,\sigma + b\,\mathbf{1} of the two-dimensional subalgebra that \sigma generates, and the trace sees it only through the scalar \mu = a\,z + b. That collapse is not unconditional. It rests on Markov stabilisation, which enters here as a hypothesis standing in for Jones' theorem rather than as something proved in place.

The proposition settles when that hypothesis may be invoked. Taking the word to be \sigma itself — the interface generator occurring a second time — the Hecke quadratic evaluates the left-hand side outright, and stabilisation collapses into a condition on z alone. The Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) misses it, and misses it by a quantity whose closed form factors into two positive-definite quadratics, q^2 \pm q + 1 = (q \pm \tfrac12)^2 + \tfrac34. The defect is therefore strictly negative at every q, not merely at the aether value; no choice of pin recovers the identity.

The consequence is a condition on the braid word rather than on the algebra. The interface scalar \mu is available exactly when the interface generator appears once. Every canonical light-nucleus word satisfies this — the deuteron and tritium use their interface generator at index 2, helium-3 and helium-4 at index 5, one occurrence each — so the collapse holds where the framework applies it. What the proposition excludes is the assumption that it would keep holding on a word built to reuse that generator.

Scope. This is a structural exclusion, and the invariant is the closed form above rather than a numerical near-miss. It constrains the shape of the word, not the choice of interface element: an element a\,\sigma + b\,\mathbf{1} remains free, and nothing here bears on which one a derivation should select.
prop:binding-functional-is-the-log:
Proposition Only the logarithmic binding functional is extensive; the linear rival fails by -\alpha(1-x)(1-y) and carries a ceiling. Write t for a trace ratio and \alpha > 0 for the energy scale. The logarithmic functional B = -\alpha \ln t is extensive,

  -\alpha \ln(xy) \;=\; -\alpha \ln x \;+\; -\alpha \ln y
  \qquad (x, y > 0),

while the linear functional B = \alpha(1 - t) fails extensivity by an exact amount,

  \alpha(1 - xy) - \bigl[\alpha(1-x) + \alpha(1-y)\bigr]
    \;=\; -\alpha\,(1-x)(1-y),

which vanishes only when x = 1 or y = 1. Separately, since the atom trace is positive, \alpha(t_{\mathrm{free}} - t_{\mathrm{atom}}) < \alpha\,t_{\mathrm{free}}.

The Markov trace is multiplicative over independent subsystems, so an atom's trace factors as t_{\mathrm{atom}} = t_{\mathrm{free}} \prod_k \mu_k over its bonds. Energy, on the other hand, is extensive. A map carrying the first structure to the second must send products to sums — Cauchy's equation on (\mathbb{R}_{>0}, \times) — whose continuous solutions are the multiples of \ln.

The proposition records the part of that argument which is mechanically checkable: of the two functionals the framework has weighed, the logarithmic one is extensive and the linear one is not. The failure is stated as an identity rather than as a measurement, so it holds at every q and needs no anchor; a bond with x = 1 contributes nothing, so on any bond that binds at all the linear form is non-extensive.

The ceiling is an independent objection and does not rely on extensivity at all. With t_{\mathrm{free}} \approx 1 across the light nuclei, the linear form cannot produce a binding energy above \alpha \approx 4.19\ \mathrm{MeV}, which already excludes {}^{3}\mathrm{H}, {}^{4}\mathrm{He} and {}^{7}\mathrm{Li} against their measured values. Two separate reasons therefore point the same way.

Scope. The uniqueness step — that Cauchy's equation admits no continuous solutions beyond c \ln x — is classical and is not proved here, so the stronger reading, that the logarithmic form is forced rather than merely preferred among the two candidates, rests on it. What is proved is the comparison. Nothing here bears on the value of \alpha, which is fixed elsewhere, nor on whether the trace ratio entering the formula is the right one.
def:nucleon-pair-isospin-channel:
Definition Colour-system selection by isospin: \mathrm{select}(p) = \mathrm{altT_1} iff T(p) = 1. The colour side of the two-nucleon interface is settled by the isotypic decomposition: an ordered pair of colour sheets carries T_1 \otimes T_1 = A \oplus T_1 \oplus H, graded by exchange as \mathrm{Sym}^2 = A \oplus H of dimension 6 and \mathrm{Alt}^2 = T_1 of dimension 3. What that decomposition leaves open is which summand a given pair of nucleons draws on. Flavour supplies the answer, because flavour is a representation too.

A nucleon pair is one of the four channels

  p \;\in\; \{\, pp,\; nn,\; pn_{\mathrm{sym}},\; pn_{\mathrm{alt}} \,\},

carrying total isospin T(pp) = T(nn) = T(pn_{\mathrm{sym}}) = 1 and T(pn_{\mathrm{alt}}) = 0, the decomposition I = \tfrac12 \otimes I = \tfrac12 \;=\; (I{=}1) \oplus (I{=}0) of dimensions 3 + 1 = 2 \times 2. The colour system of a pair is the summand of T_1 \otimes T_1 its interface draws on, one of \mathrm{altT_1} = T_1 or \mathrm{symAH} = A \oplus H. The selection map is

  \mathrm{select}(p) \;=\;
  \begin{cases}
    \mathrm{altT_1}, & T(p) = 1, \\[2pt]
    \mathrm{symAH},  & T(p) = 0 .
  \end{cases}

What the map encodes

Two couplings and no others carry overall antisymmetry under simultaneous exchange of the colour-sheet and flavour labels: exchange-symmetric flavour with the antisymmetric colour summand, and exchange-antisymmetric flavour with the symmetric one. The map above is that pairing written out. The hypothesis that the physical interface realises it is a named physical assumption, not a theorem --- nucleon-level Fermi statistics constrains the full wavefunction, space \otimes spin \otimes isospin \otimes colour, and not this sub-sector in isolation --- and it is carried as a conjecture class with no registered instance, so every consequence drawn from it stays conditional.

Three consequences follow immediately once the class is assumed. The like-nucleon channels pp and nn both sit in I = 1, so the interface assigns them the same colour system and charge symmetry becomes a consequence of the rule rather than a constraint imposed on it. The T_1 summand carries no residual freedom, its normalised weights being 0 on same-colour pairs and 1/6 on each different-colour pair, so the entire I = 1 sector is determined. Only the deuteron channel retains a parameter, the A-versus-H mix inside \mathrm{Sym}^2.

The charge-symmetry consequence carries one caveat. It follows because the construction is organised by isospin and pp, nn are isospin conjugates, so any isospin-covariant weighting is charge-symmetric. The content of the observation is that the production \sigma-versus-\sigma^{-1} assignment is not isospin-covariant, which is the diagnosed charge-symmetry-breaking defect; it is not an independent coincidence.

A fourth consequence is less obvious: the symmetric pn channel groups with the like-nucleon pairs rather than with the deuteron. The pn pair splits, its I = 1 component weighted exactly as pp and nn are, and only its I = 0 component free.
rem:isospin-selection-class-inhabited:
Remark \mathrm{InterfaceExchangeAntisymmetry} is inhabited by \langle\mathrm{select},\,\mathrm{rfl}\rangle --- the class carries physics, not a constraint. The selection rule is carried by a conjecture class with two fields: a coupling assigning a colour system to each nucleon-pair channel, and the constraint that the coupling equals \mathrm{select}. Stated that way the class is inhabited by construction. Taking the coupling to be \mathrm{select} itself and the constraint to be reflexivity exhibits a witness, so the class constrains nothing as a mathematical object.

The opposite was previously asserted. A class whose only field is pinned to a definition already in scope cannot fail to be satisfiable, and an argument that leaned on its non-vacuity would be leaning on nothing.

What remains open, and why it is not vacuity

The class does not assert that some coupling satisfies the rule. It asserts that the coupling induced by the physical interface is \mathrm{select}. No formal inhabitation can establish that, and none is claimed: what the witness shows is that the mathematical content of the class is empty, leaving its physical content intact and entirely unproved. The four consequences drawn from it therefore stay conditional --- charge symmetry between pp and nn, the forcing of the like-nucleon channels onto T_1, the freeing of the deuteron channel alone, and the grouping of the symmetric pn state with the like-nucleon pairs --- but the hypothesis they wait on is a physical identification, not an open theorem.

Inhabitation is recorded as a statement about non-emptiness and deliberately not as a typeclass instance. Registering an instance would let resolution discharge the hypothesis automatically, silently converting all four conditional theorems into unconditional statements about \mathrm{select}. Those statements would be true, they would follow by evaluating a two-line table, and they would be worthless --- while reading, to anyone scanning the file, as though the physics had been proved. Keeping the fact as a non-emptiness statement records it without changing what anything downstream depends on.
prop:branching-identity-isospin-weights:
Proposition \mu_+ = y_{(3)} + y_{(2,1)}, \mu_- = y_{(2,1)} + y_{(1^3)} --- hence at z = q^3/(q^2+1) the singlet draws nothing from the radical. Let \mathrm{tr}_M be any Markov trace on H_3(q), expanded in the Wedderburn basis as y_{(3)}\chi^{(3)} + y_{(2,1)}\chi^{(2,1)} + y_{(1^3)}\chi^{(1^3)} and normalised by \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1, \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma) = z. Then the two isospin scalars are sums over the H_2(q) \subset H_3(q) branching,

  \mu_+ \;=\; y_{(3)} + y_{(2,1)},
  \qquad
  \mu_- \;=\; y_{(2,1)} + y_{(1^3)},

identically in z and in q. At z = q^3/(q^2+1), where y_{(1^3)} = 0, the singlet weight is therefore \mu_- = y_{(2,1)} exactly.

Where the two sums come from

Restriction along H_2(q) \subset H_3(q) branches each Young diagram of 3 into the diagrams of 2 obtained by removing a box. The totally symmetric shape (3) restricts entirely to the symmetric shape (2); the totally antisymmetric shape (1^3) restricts entirely to (1^2); and the mixed shape (2,1), being two-dimensional, reaches both. Reading the Bratteli diagram off in that order gives exactly the two displayed sums, with y_{(2,1)} appearing on each side for the plain reason that \dim(2,1) = 2.

The two normalisations are all that is needed to prove them. Writing out \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1 and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma) = z against the character values \chi(1) = (1,2,1) and \chi(\sigma) = (q,\, q-q^{-1},\, -q^{-1}), the combination -\mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma) - q^{-1}\mathrm{tr}_M(1) cancels y_{(1^3)} and yields z + q^{-1} = (q+q^{-1})(y_{(3)} + y_{(2,1)}), while \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma) - q\,\mathrm{tr}_M(1) cancels y_{(3)} and yields q - z = (q+q^{-1})(y_{(2,1)} + y_{(1^3)}). No convention is chosen, no value of q is fixed, and no fit enters; both are instances of the three-term branching recursion.

A corollary of the same reading is that \mu_+ + \mu_- = 1 carries no information about isospin. On the \mu side the sum is vacuous --- the z cancels with no hypotheses at all --- and on the branch side it is y_{(3)} + 2y_{(2,1)} + y_{(1^3)} = \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1, the normalisation restated. Any Markov trace whatever satisfies it.

The radical is observationally inert

At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the antisymmetric weight vanishes identically, so the second sum collapses to a single term and the isospin singlet draws its entire weight from the mixed-symmetry block. Quotienting H_3(q) by its radical deletes a summand that was already contributing zero. More generally a term with y_\lambda = 0 can be removed from \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \chi^\lambda without changing any value, so the radical is invisible to every trace and hence to every observable the framework computes from one.

That is what makes the repair demanded by the degeneracy obstruction free. The obstruction is real --- a degenerate form gives the Lipschitz seminorm a kernel and the Connes distance is unbounded --- and the quotient that removes it costs no physics.

The isospin weights are the two-strand weights

One further identification falls out of the same branching. At z = q^3/(q^2+1) the two isospin scalars are the Wedderburn weights of H_2(q) itself,

  \mu_+ \;=\; y_{(2)}\bigl[H_2\bigr],
  \qquad
  \mu_- \;=\; y_{(1,1)}\bigl[H_2\bigr],

and the two numbers the nucleon-pair sector runs on are therefore not new data attached to H_3(q) but the weights of the two-strand algebra seen one level up. This is the edge that fixes where the Temperley--Lieb characterisation belongs: it is a statement about the tower, and it is developed with the algebra rather than with the physics that consumes it.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs --- real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the aether parameter q_0. Any generic categorical or q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here. At q_0 the three descriptions of the singlet weight agree to every digit carried: \mu_- = (q_0-z)/(q_0+q_0^{-1}), y_{(2,1)} = 1/[2]_{q_0}^{2}, and the product \mu_{pp}\,\mu_{nn} = 1/(q_0+q_0^{-1})^{2} all evaluate to 0.24729788674803459841.
prop:interface-band-between-isospin-weig:
Proposition The admissible interface band [z-h,\,z] lies strictly between \mu_- and \mu_+. Let \mu = z + d with d \in [-h,\,0] be an admissible interface scalar, so that \mu ranges over the band [z-h,\,z]. At z = q^3/(q^2+1), whenever the two reduced inequalities

  q - z \;<\; (z-h)\,(q+q^{-1}),
  \qquad
  z\,(q+q^{-1}) \;<\; z + q^{-1}

  \boxed{\;\; \mu_- \;<\; \mu \;<\; \mu_+ . \;\;}

cor:interface-never-realises-isospin-wei:
Corollary No admissible interface element realises either isospin weight: the two mechanisms compute on disjoint sets. Under the hypotheses of the band separation, every admissible interface scalar \mu = z + d with d \in [-h,\,0] satisfies

  \mu \;\ne\; \mu_-
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \mu \;\ne\; \mu_+ .

Strict inequalities on both sides give the two non-equalities directly. Stated this way the result is the sharpest form of the obstruction: it is not that the interface reproduces an isospin weight badly, it is that the interface never reproduces one at all.

Two mechanisms, disjoint ranges

The isospin mechanism selects the bound channel and the interface mechanism produces the binding number, and it has never been shown that they are the same object. The corollary settles that they are not. The values the interface can take form the interval [z-h,\, z]; the values isospin assigns are the two points \mu_- and \mu_+; and the interval separates the points without containing either. Using the T = 0 projector as the interface element is therefore not an unmotivated choice; it is an unavailable one.

What a repair would have to change

The obstruction was first posed as a dimension count: the bond family \mathrm{span}\{1, \sigma_2\} reaches only a 2-plane of the four-dimensional V_{(2,1)} block. The present statement is the same obstruction read on the observable side, where it becomes quantitative --- the two targets miss the reachable interval by 63.22\,\% and 22.85\,\%.

That reading also says what will not work. Tuning d moves a point inside an interval that does not contain the target; choosing a crossing sign selects an endpoint of the same interval; choosing a different q moves both endpoints and both targets together, and the margins are wide enough that no admissible q closes them. A repair must change the arena. Two candidates remain open: enlarging H_3(q) to H_4(q), which widens the reachable set from 2 to 5 parameters inside a nine-dimensional block, or pairing the isospin label to the bond in some way other than identifying the projector with the interface. Neither is carried out here, and the first carries its own risk --- three extra parameters that are not themselves derived would convert a clean impossibility into a fit with room to hide.
rem:colour-tube-floor-overshoots-deutero:
Remark The colour-tube selection rule cannot supply the interface tilt: a category error, corroborated by a family floor above the deuteron. The colour-tube channel weight is a natural candidate for the interface tilt d: it already assigns a rational weight to each pair of colour sheets, it is normalised, and it is upstream of the same D_6 structure the interface sits in. It cannot supply the tilt, and the reason is a category error rather than a numerical miss.

The category error

The colour-tube weight is a function W_{c_1c_2}(F_1, F_2) of two colour sheets and two nucleon colour contents, where a content is a definite assignment of a quark flavour to each of the three sheets --- (u,u,d) for the proton, (u,d,d) for the neutron. The chirality sign it is built from compares F_1 at sheet c_1 against F_2 at sheet c_2, so the whole construction presupposes that each nucleon of the pair has a definite flavour content.

The deuteron does not. Its flavour state is the antisymmetric line (pn - np)/\sqrt2, on which F_1 and F_2 are not definite: the state is a superposition of the two content assignments, and the weight is not a linear functional on the flavour space but a function of the labels. Evaluating W_{c_1c_2} on the deuteron therefore requires a choice of branch that the construction does not supply, and any such choice breaks the exchange antisymmetry that defines the channel. The obstruction is structural: it is a property of what the weight is allowed to depend on, exactly as in the content-keyed refutation, and no adjustment of the weights repairs it.

The numerical corroboration, and what backs it

Independently of the above, the family the rule generates has been scanned for the pn binding it would predict. The figures in this paragraph are provisional: they are recorded from an exploratory scan and are not yet reproduced by a committed producer, so no witness backs them. Scanning the mixing parameter on a hundredth grid across the six colour alignments at thirty digits gives a family floor of B_{pn} = 2.29580\ \mathrm{MeV}, against the measured B_{\mathrm{AME}}({}^2\mathrm{H}) = 2.224566\ \mathrm{MeV} --- an overshoot of 0.0712\ \mathrm{MeV}, or 3.2\,\%, by the most favourable member of the family. The S_3 average that confinement demands lands higher still, at 2.46755\ \mathrm{MeV}, some 11\,\% above target. Reaching the measured value requires a mixing parameter of 0.35768, which is to say it requires knowing the answer first.

The two arguments are of different kinds and should not be conflated. The category error excludes the construction outright; the scan reports that this family, on its own and on the grid scanned, does not reach the target. The scan is corroboration, and it is the weaker of the two.

Convergence with the band separation

Three independent routes now arrive at the same wall. The interface band lies strictly between the two isospin weights, so no admissible element realises either; the colour-tube family's floor sits above the deuteron; and the content-keyed proposal is refuted by the two pn channels. Each closes a different way of trying to derive the tilt from structure already in hand, and none of them is closed by a better parameter. What they leave standing is the arena question: whether widening the algebra, rather than re-weighting inside it, is where the tilt comes from.
